title: Derived inverse image of open extension vanishes on a disjoint image
statement: Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring and Lambda_T = p_T^* Lambda. Let j : U -> X be an open immersion and g : Z -> X any scheme morphism whose set-theoretic image is disjoint from that of j. For every object K of the unbounded derived category of Lambda_U-module objects on U_proet, the object Lg^*(j_! K) is zero. Here j_! is the levelwise derived exact module extension by zero. No quasi-compactness, properness, constructibility or boundedness is assumed. The coefficient categories and functors are those of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

proof.text: For every pro-etale object T -> U the fibre product T x_X Z is empty: a point would map to both disjoint images. Sections of an abelian sheaf on an empty site object form the zero object. Therefore j^*g_*M is zero on underlying abelian sheaves, and the coefficient pullback isomorphism transports the calculation to module objects. The underlying module inverse image is identified using the existing profinitePointModuleForgetPullbackIso from Sheaf.Paper.ProfinitePointPullback; no duplicate forgetful-pullback definition is introduced.

proof.text: Module inverse image is exact because alpha_g is invertible and underlying inverse image is exact; open extension is exact. Their levelwise derived functors commute with homology, so the preceding underived zero calculation makes every homology object of their composite zero. A derived object with zero homology is zero. The exact-functor comparison identifies levelwise inverse image with Lg^*. This includes the empty open and zero complex.
